about: What cannot be scored from [Fock] here, one record each: claim, mechanism, evidence, asserted_value, source. See felizjueves.literature.limits. Milestone 12 scores no published cell: there is no tables.json in this directory, by decision (pin 2).

limits.claim: No [Fock] table is a scoreboard here. In the text read (arXiv v1), Tables 1 and 2 are single-A100 Fock-build speedups of opt-Brc and opt-UM over TeraChem, QUICK and GPU4PySCF; Table 3 is single-iteration K timings in seconds on a V100 against LibintX; Table 4 is SCF iteration timings in seconds on 1 and 4 A100s. Milestone 12's 'Table 3, A100 seconds' is the journal version's numbering, which this reading could not see; the preprint's Table 4 fits that description, and the conclusion is the same for every table.
limits.mechanism: Every table is a wall-clock measurement (or a ratio of two) of whole programs on hardware this box does not have: an A100 or a V100, against an RTX 3080 (sm_86) and an RX 9060 XT (gfx1200). A timing depends on the card, the compiler and the rest of the program, none of which a reconstruction of §3 describes, so no model or kernel here predicts one.
limits.evidence: Table captions of arXiv:2407.21445v1, read for this record (#271). Milestone 12 pin 2: one literature file, no table cells; no tables.json is added under data/literature/fock/, and test/test_fock_coverage.py holds that.

limits.claim: §6's benchmarks (Figs. 5-9: single-GPU comparisons, strong scaling on 1-4 A100s, CPU comparisons, J/K scaling and per-class timings) are not reproduced or scored.
limits.mechanism: They are whole-program wall-clock on NERSC Perlmutter nodes (AMD EPYC 7763, four A100 40 GB or 80 GB), against other packages this repo does not run. This repo builds the two-electron F of §3's kernel, not an SCF program, and has neither the hardware nor the comparators.
limits.evidence: §6's opening paragraph and figure captions, arXiv:2407.21445v1 (#271).

limits.claim: There is no published register table for the §3.2 kernel: the paper reports no register count, spill figure or occupancy for any opt-Brc class, so milestone 12's generated F kernel has no published figure to be held to. The predecessor's hand-spelled kernel (its test/hgp/brc/ptxas_data.py, measured under nvcc 13.0, -arch=sm_86) is a quality baseline of common ancestry (#289), never a witness and never a [Fock] cell.
limits.mechanism: Registers and spills are compiler readings of one kernel text on one architecture; the paper prints only timings, and mentions registers only qualitatively (§2.3's register pressure; §6's 80 GB cards 'to accommodate' f-function spills).
limits.evidence: A search of arXiv:2407.21445v1 for 'register' finds §2.3, §4.2, §4.3.2, §4.4 and §6 prose and no table (#271); the predecessor records the same absence.

limits.claim: Milestone 12 moves no [JEngine] cell, floor, claim or status. [Fock] was already a reference here (docs/references.md entry 23), cited as prior art in ao/k.py and kernel_k.py ([Fock, §4.3.1], [Fock, §4.3.2]); this directory is the first time a section of it is reconstructed rather than cited, and its records are its own.
limits.mechanism: [JEngine] is J only and its board is Tables 1-3 of that paper; [Fock] §3 is another engine (HGP, fused F) with no table cell this repo can score. The two registries are checked per paper (felizjueves.literature.claims.load_registry), so neither reads the other's records.
limits.evidence: #271 adds data/literature/fock/ and touches no file under data/literature/jengine/ or data/scoreboards/; test/test_claims.py checks each paper's registry separately.

limits.claim: The efficacy of §3.2's screens (eq. 29's pre-launch batch-pair screen and the six-block in-kernel screen) is not measured: how much work they remove depends on how extended the molecule is, and every fixture here is compact.
limits.mechanism: A Schwarz or density screen removes quartets in proportion to the fraction of distant pairs; in H2, H2O and HF that fraction is small, so a measured saving would be a fact about the fixture, not about the screen (milestone 12 pin 9). An extended case is a follow-up.
limits.evidence: Milestone 12 pin 9; the fixture list in test/oracle/fixtures/.
